# nonNegative

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a number that is not negative.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNegative() — Checks whether a value is a number that is not negative. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.0.0 · <b>Deprecated</b></p>
</tldr>

> **Deprecated.** Use [`isNonNegative`](isNonNegative.md) instead, which says the same thing under the naming convention used across the library. This alias is kept for backwards compatibility and will be removed in a future major release.

```typescript
function nonNegative(value: unknown): value is number;
```

The name breaks the convention the rest of the library follows: everywhere else a `nonX` prefix means “is not X”, and here it means “is a non-negative number”. `isNonNegative` says the same thing under the right name and is what new code should call.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a number and is not negative.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `number` inside the branch.

## Examples

### In use

```javascript
nonNegative(0); // => true
nonNegative(-1); // => false
```
